title: Collections Review: Pick the Right Tool
story: Your team lead drops five feature requests on your desk: a leaderboard, a user profile store, a spam filter, a message queue, and a settings dictionary. Each one needs a different data structure. Pick wrong and you'll fight your data all week. Pick right and the code writes itself.
why: Choosing Vec vs Map vs Set is a fundamental design decision — each excels at different data shapes, and knowing which to use prevents hours of rework.
analogy: Choosing a collection is like choosing a tool from a toolbox. A hammer (Vec) drives nails in order. A labeled filing cabinet (Map) lets you grab any file by its label instantly. A unique-item tray (Set) rejects duplicates. You wouldn't use a hammer to file paperwork, and you wouldn't use a filing cabinet to drive nails. Pick the tool that matches the job.
try_it: For each scenario below, decide: Vec, Map, or Set? (1) A music playlist with song order. (2) A dictionary for spell-checking. (3) A list of unique email subscribers. (4) A phone book (name → number). (5) A browser tab history (back/forward). Then implement all five in one program.
tips: Ask: 'Do I need order?' → Vec. 'Do I need key→value lookup?' → Map. 'Do I need uniqueness?' → Set.
Sometimes you need TWO collections: Vec for order + Map for fast lookup by ID
Start with Vec (simplest), switch to Map or Set the moment you feel pain from scanning or duplicates
common_mistakes: Using Vec for key-value lookups — scanning a Vec for 'Alice' in 10,000 entries is painfully slow vs Map
Using Map when you only care about existence — Map stores values you don't need; Set is cleaner
Using Set for something that needs ordering — Set doesn't preserve insertion order
